articleTitle: On the Perspectives of Graduated Engineering Students on Three Dimensions of the Integrated Curriculum from a Peruvian University
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The integrated curriculum is made up of five dimensions: knowledge, internships, counseling, the arts and sports and research. The University of Sciences and Humanities (in Spanish: Universidad de Ciencias y Humanidades; UCH) from Lima, Peru at the core of the curricula of their different faculties follows the integrated training model in order to shape ideal professionals. In order to gain an insight into how the faculty from science and engineering at the UCH is handling three dimensions (internships, the arts and sports and research) of the integrated training model, a survey was carried out among graduated students from the electronic engineering and computer science programs. We could discover that overall, there is a good degree of satisfaction among the electronic engineering graduates with all the three aforementioned dimensions. However, in the case of the computer science graduates a discrepancy with regard to these three dimensions could be observed. In view of these results, a new survey is planned to shed more light into the difference of the perpectives among these two groups. On the other hand considering the obtained results, we suggest (and it is already planned) that the faculty of science and engineering from the UCH gives more internships opportunities to their current students, and also intensifies the research dimension, for instance, with the implementation of hotbeds of research. This will further benefit the students to become better professionals and also will support the faculty of science and engineering from the UCH when looking for accreditation of its two programs with the Latin American accreditation agency ICACIT.

articleTitle: Assessment of student outcomes for the ICACIT accreditation: An Industrial Engineering case study
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Working on the continuous improvement of the quality of undergraduate programs is a priority for universities around the world, and for that purpose, several accrediting agencies are responsible for verifying the achievement of high quality standards. This paper provides details of the assessment procedure of student outcome (SO) related to the Industrial Engineering degree program of Universidad Privada del Norte. The evaluation was conducted by using instruments based on measuring rubrics that are designed for students as well as surveys designed for graduates and employers. The data collected from these sources are aggregated and analyzed to quantify the achievement of the student outcomes. Rates for students of 81.7% ± 7.81, graduates 98.17% ± 2.55 and employers 94.58% ± 4.16, form the basis for the activities of the continuous improvement process in the Industrial Engineering degree program. This study provides details about the measurement procedure for student outcomes and serves to demonstrate an educational practice for the process of accreditation in an engineering degree program.

articleTitle: M-Learning applied to the improvement of the learning of university engineering students
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This paper is intended to determine the extent to which the M-learning model with methodological strategies improves the learning of student’s undergraduates of the Systems Engineering career. The method used was developed through a study of quasi-experimental type and conformed by an experimental group composed of 25 students of section B and a control group by 25 students of section A of the subject of Software Design Patterns. of the Autonomous University of Peru. To obtain the results of the inferential analysis, the Student T test and the Mann Whitney U test were used. Likewise, a prestest and a posttest were applied to evidence the learning improved, previously tests of validity and reliability were performed in each case, the corresponding calculations were subsequently made for the test of the hypotheses. After applying the M-learning model with methodological strategies, significant differences were observed (p = 0.000 <0.05) in the general, declarative, procedural and attitudinal learning, in the results of the pretest and posttest evaluation, being higher the average of the posttest, with a 95% level of confidence. With the results obtained, we can conclude that the M-learning model with methodological strategies significantly improves the learning of university students of the Systems Engineering career of the Autonomous University of Perú in the subject of Software Design Patterns.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Networks to optimize learning and teaching in engineering careers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This article presents how Artificial Intelligence can improve the ways of learning and teaching on the field of Engineering. The main problem we want to face takes place in Education and it shares a common root with the low development of technology applied to this area. In this document, we explain about how tools like artificial neural networks and Artificial Intelligence can improve the situation of Education, providing an efficient alternative to make the students increase their levels of learning to perform well as professionals after finishing their studies of higher education. From the side of teachers, we implement evaluations for them, to verify how much they contribute in the learning process to their students. All of these functionalities are contemplated in the system that we describe in this document, with the main purpose of change the classic paradigms of Education, introducing technology in benefit of the universitary community.

articleTitle: Matlab Mobile as a Support Tool for The Performance of Students in Engineering
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Based on a quasi-experimental study, this paper analyzes MATLAB MOBILE software as a support tool for academic performance in the subject of teaching numerical methods, algorithms and programming languages for engineering students. The decision was made to address this problem with a sample of 84 students among the groups for different semesters studying the aforementioned subject. From work as a teacher, based on observations and information recorded in the records of the school services department, it is necessary to look for new strategies for academic improvement; because the results obtained from the average of this subject show ups and downs during the years 2015 to 2018, because the average obtained is 16 in relation to the maximum score of 20 for the achievement of the expected competition, which means that they do not bring bases for the development of skills and abilities to learn to program and interpret algorithms. The work done in front of the group of students, allows observing that when asking the student to solve a problem using a programming language, they present difficulties, which causes that they do not wake up in them, the interest to solve them through the programming, seen this way The programming tool that combines the features to solve the problem is MATLAB MOBILE. Reason why, the purpose of this work is to demonstrate, how the MATLAB MOBILE integrating software in the aforementioned subject can contribute to increase comprehension and academic performance.

articleTitle: Key factors to consider prior to the start of an accreditation project
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This document compiles and organizes learnings and practices as a guide for those institutions that decide to start an accreditation project, regardless of the accrediting entity they have selected for it. Each one of the six factors considered as key is described as a product of the experience of the Engineering School of the University of Piura, whose four academic programs have followed accreditation processes with two institutions: Sineace and Icacit.

articleTitle: Compliance Assessment of ISO 21001:2018 Clause 8.5 in the Systems Engineering Program of Universidad Autónoma del Perú
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The Universidad Autónoma del Perú (UA) implemented its Quality Management System in 2015 achieving the ISO 9001: 2015 certification in February 2019. This certification covers all the processes related to student support services, laboratories, degrees and diplomas among others. Due the specificity for educational organizations of ISO 21001: 2018 standard, the UA considered to align the current management system with the ISO 21001: 2018 requirements, beginning with the Systems Engineering Program. This paper displays the methodology and the results of the compliance assessment of the existing processes against the ISO 21001: 2018 Clause 8.5 in February 2019. As a result, it was found that the current management system meets the common requirements between ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 21001:2018. Nevertheless, there are some breaches in Clauses 8.5.1, 8.5. 2, 8.5.3, 8.5.5 and 8.5.6. Finally, the corresponding gaps were identified and the respective continuous improvement plans were developed.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Capstone Project Courses of diverse specialties in a School of Engineering in Lima
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The capstone project course at the end of the engineering program curriculum is a very special learning space. However, this must respond to intentional pedagogical design. This article presents a comparative analysis of capstone projects courses of 5 engineering programs in Lima from the professor's perspective. The way in which the courses are carried out allows or affects the achievement of the proposed objectives of the course. In this analysis, we identified influential factors to meet goals and lesson learned.

articleTitle: Self-Efficacy And Its Effect On Anxiety And Performance In Mathematics In Aspiring to Career in Engineering
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The present investigation takes as an intention to analyze the mathematical self-efficacy and its relation with the mathematical anxiety, the anxiety before evaluations and the academic performance in pre-university students who aspire to study engineering career in a public university of Peru. The sample had 61 pre university students candidates to the engineering careers (28 men (45.9%) and 33 women (54.1%)) between 15 and 26 years old (M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">age</sup> = 17.82, SD = 1.76). The results showed, that in the women major anxiety level exists before mathematical examinations. It was observed in the regressions analysis that it was confirmed that the mathematical self-efficacy predicts negatively to the anxiety before the examinations and before the study of the mathematics; and he predicts positively to the academic performance. Then the regressions analysis demonstrated that the anxiety before the mathematics examinations is decisive to predict negatively the academic performance.

articleTitle: Internships within the curriculum and their importance as a bridge to the job market
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The search for the first job related to the professional career is a problem that is found among many university students in Peru. This is mainly due to the lack of professional experience of the student, which is percieved by the students creating a barrier for themselves. This article refers to the importance of internships within the study grid and the relationship it has with the level of employability of graduates. For this, it has been studied what is the impact of internships on students. Using a type and design of descriptive, correlational and cross-sectional research, with a value of Pearson's correlation coefficient = 0.995, it can be deduced that there is a positive linear correlation between the number of graduates and the level of employability of these in the Faculty of Sciences and Engineering of the Sciences and Humanities University between 2014 and 2018.

articleTitle: Curriculum Design Process for a Systems Engineering Program
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This paper describes the activities developed in a curriculum reflection process and the preliminary results obtained so far. The process is based on the CDIO integrated curriculum design approach but involves other elements such us ABET accreditation guidelines, disciplinary referents and the Quality model for the program, already in place. The process to define the Program Educational Objectives and Student Outcomes, as described by ABET, is explained. Student outcomes encompasses both: disciplinary and personal and interpersonal skills, and product, process, and system building skills. Learning expected levels are established for each outcome. A proposal is presented on how to manage the relation between the new ABET student outcomes (labeled 1-7) and the new general student outcomes defined by the program. Preliminary decisions about the curricular structure are also discussed. The process of defining the sequence of content and learning outcomes using backward design, is presented.

articleTitle: Assessment and Evaluation of the Student Outcomes and Formulation of Improvement Plans for an Engineering Academic Program
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The following work describes the used methodology for the definition of the processes of Assessment and Evaluation of the Student Outcomes and the subprocesses of Formulation, Review and Approval of Improvement Plans for an Engineering Academic Program. The main concepts, the methodology used and the results obtained are defined, as well as the conclusions and recommendations resulting from the experience of the Engineering School of the University of Piura.

articleTitle: Integrating project-based learning in an Electrical Machines course
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This article describes the teaching-learning method implementation “project-based learning” PBL on a university chair. It was sought that the students through real-life situations acquire knowledge, skills, and attitudes within the subject of Electrical Machines at the undergraduate level of Electrical Engineering at the Catholic University of Cuenca. The resolution problems of static machines were similar to those on professional life. The students had the ability to identify a static machine, operation, parameters, equivalent circuits (tests in open-circuit and short-circuit), losses calculation, and the hysteresis cycle data. Because these concepts are abstract and difficult to assimilate for them. For this reason, this research demonstrates the best learning performance of students. The PBL applied to the learning of static machines is a good teaching tool. An improvement of 7 points out of 100 was obtained in relation to the average of the scores of three students groups from previous semesters. Moreover, the standard deviation is lower in the experimental group (SD 4.5584). This shows that the best performance was present in most of the students. In this way, the students not lost the scholastic year, nor there was a supplementary exam in this group.

articleTitle: Quality managenent of university education for the development of soft skills in the engineering program
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This research is a methodological proposal to facilitate the implementation of a system that manages quality control in university education for the development of soft skills in the Industrial Engineering Program in the peruvian university, which in turn ensures compliance with University Law No. 30220 regarding the quality improvement.With this methodology, we hope to contribute to the promotion of quality integral training in the Industrial Engineering Program in peruvian universities, which is so necessary to make that great leap that is required to make our country, a country of integral citizens.

articleTitle: Use of a PID controller adjustment graphic interface, to improve student assessments in an engineering course
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: With the use of a Graphical Interface developed in Matlab software, for the tuning of Proportional (P), Proportional-Integral (PI) and Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) type controllers, by the Tanteo method [2], it was possible to reach a significant progress in the evaluations of the students enrolled in the course Control Engineering for the academic cycles 2018-1 and 2018-2, in the career of Electronic Engineering of the Ricardo Palma University. This interface made it possible to visualize in an animated way the result of the tuning of the controllers, thus allowing the students to complement the theoretical topics taught in the classroom during laboratory hours. In this way, when comparing the results of the evaluations of the partial exams and the final grade of the period 2015 to 2017, with respect to the year 2018, we observed an improvement in the students' assessments, obtaining an increase of the average of 10.22 at 12.54 with a standard deviation less than and equal to 1.3060, and an increase in the median from 10.29 to 12.54.

articleTitle: Didactic module of temperature control with Labview, to support the teaching in engineering subject
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This article describes the implementation of a didactic module for temperature control for the latest laboratory experiences in the subject: Instrumentation and Process Control, belonging to the eighth cycle of the Electronic Engineering Degree at the Ricardo Palma University. For this implementation, a power circuit was designed that represented the actuator, and by means of which it was possible to manipulate the AC current intensity for the gradual on/off of the lamps inside the wooden educational module, which represented the plant. In addition, an intelligent temperature transmitter and a programming routine made in the Demo version of Labview were used to algorithmically represent the On-Off, Proportional, Proportional-Integral controller. The interaction of the temperature transmitter and the power module with the controller was done through a data acquisition card from National Instruments. In this way, with the experience of the dictation of this subject for twenty-three academic semesters, between 2004 y 2016, the temperature didactic module was improved progressing and has supported teaching, achieving a gradual increase in the laboratory evaluations of the students who attended throughout that period.

articleTitle: Postgraduates in Engineering and its Relationship with Teaching Quality
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This paper presents a proposal on the determinants of quality teaching in postgraduate courses for Engineering, using mixed methodology techniques to identify and explain its most important factors, being a context little explored. The following aspects are recognized: institutional environment, theoretical-practical course balance, teaching research experience, student characteristics, tutoring and research paper, adding these elements to the evaluation analysis, which differ in different levels of the variables commonly analyzed in undergraduate. It is established that these factors are interrelated and must be considered in an exclusive teacher evaluation methodology for postgraduates that actually measures the training characteristics associated with this level.

articleTitle: Multiple Adoption of Program Accreditation Models and Campus Licence: An University Experience
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: To starts quality actions using external references as university or programs accreditation models is always a good idea. However, in the effort to adopt two or more models in a simultaneous way, it is necessary identify model's requirements that are similar; and requirements that are specific to each program; being necessary to organize in a corporate way the effort of all stakeholders. The objective of this article is to present the strategies adopted in relation to the achievements obtained. In the article, we discuss, based on experience, how these strategies were adopted according to each model. The strategies adopted allowing us to achieve the goals and perform a job with the least possible duplicity and reducing confusion of using multiple models.

articleTitle: On the Impact of Mathematics in a First Year Algorithms Course of a Computer Science Program in a University of Lima, Peru
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Algorithms are considered as one of the foundations of computer science. In all the computer science programs around the world they are offered as a core course of their curricula. However, in order to write algorithms a good knowledge and understanding of mathematics is needed. It is then the purpose of this study to show how the performance of the students in the course of algorithms of the computer science program offered at the University of Sciences and Humanities (Lima, Peru) is affected by their performance in the course of mathematics offered at that same program. The period of study covered four years, from 2015 to 2018, making a total of 8 semesters. The performance indicators in both courses were the average of the final grades of the students in each course per semester. A positive moderate correlation between the grades in mathematics and the ones in the algorithms course was calculated. Additionally, a linear model which shows the dependence between these two variables (i.e., the averages of the final grades of the courses of mathematics and algorithms per semester) was determined. On the other hand, we have observed the performance in these same courses which were offered alternatively following a hybrid system (traditional+virtual classroom) during the 2018-II semester. Because the performance of the students in this hybrid system is better than the ones from the traditional classroom (2015-I to 2018-II) we suggest that some of the techniques used in the hybrid system should be applied (and will be) starting the new semester of 2019-I to the traditional classroom courses of mathematics and algorithms.

articleTitle: Self-Assessment of the Computer Engineering Career at the Universidad Americana
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The accreditation of Higher Education careers aims to certify the quality of the educational offer. This paper presents a summary of the result of the self-assessment process developed in the Computer Engineering Career at the Universidad Americana, through the National Model of Higher Education Accreditation, established by the National Agency for the Evaluation and Accreditation of Higher Education, The result of the process strengthened teamwork between teachers and university authorities in order to verify compliance with the quality criteria defined for the accreditation of degree courses in Paraguay.

articleTitle: Métodos de Decisión Multi-Criterio aplicados al proceso de evaluación de las carreras de Ingenierias
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The evaluation becomes the fundamental axis from which the improvement plans are developed, because it considers a series of assumptions duly supported that contemplate the historical evolution of the results of each one of the indicators. Therefore, this article discusses how the implementation of the race self-evaluation, specifically the multi-criterion decision methods and the utility curves applied to the engineering area allow to improve the processes by more than 50%; Becoming a tool for managers in the planning of their careers.

articleTitle: Performance of female students of a Peruvian engineering faculty in their first two year formative research courses
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This research presents the results obtained by 6 groups of female students, in relation to their academic performance in courses related to formative research, which make up Program I of the Faculty of Engineering from the University of Sciences and Humanities. The averages obtained in each of the courses were taken into account, and compared with those obtained by their male peers. We could discover that the academic performance of female students is better in each of the courses that make up program I of formative research.

articleTitle: Study of the relevance of an engineering program from the model of viable systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to select the components to study the relevance of an engineering program, for this, the program accreditation model, the diagnostic model of the program, and the methods of updating the requirements of the interested parties must be defined. The methodology has been applied to the Electronic Engineering Program of the UNPRG, having chosen the ICACIT Accreditation Model, the Viable Systems Model for the diagnosis of the program and the DACUM Methods for the constituents of the near environment and the DELPHI Method for the intermediate and global constituents and opinions of experts on the future of Electronic engineering. The advances to the present are favorable, the identification of the levels of recursion, of the systems of the model and the companies of the near surroundings were concluded.

articleTitle: Engagement and Academic Self-efficacy in Engineering Students of a Public University in Lima-Peru. A Correlational Study
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This research work is based on a sample of 53 engineering students from a public university in Lima-Peru, and aims to analyze the correlations between academic self-efficacy and the four components of engagement (behavioral, emotional, cognitive and agentic). The results revealed that only three of these components (behavioral, emotional and cognitive) maintain a positive and significant relationship with academic self-efficacy. Therefore, it is concluded that, unlike studies conducted based on other samples, participation in class (or agentic component) does not necessarily ensure academic self-efficacy in engineering students.

articleTitle: Elaboration of didactic handbook with Matlab, to strengthen teaching-learning process in introductory subject of telecommunications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This article shows the procedure made for the elaboration of a didactic handbook using the Matlab, for the subject Telecommunications I of the sixth academic semester in the Electronics engineering career, of the Faculty of Engineering of the Ricardo Palma University. Therefore, based on the content of the syllabus, several examples and exercises were chosen and developed with simulations of the topics of this subject; as, for example: representation of periodic and non-periodic signals, application of analog filters, representation of the Series and the Fourier Transform, and analog modulation/demodulation AM, FM and PM. Also, with the experience in the dictation of the hours of theory and practice of this subject, from the academic semester 2010-1 to date, averages of the qualified practices as evolution of time were plotted and a substantial increment of the result of such evaluations was obtained, showing a positive slope equal to 0.2965.

articleTitle: Admission options and their implications for student desertion at the National University of Engineering
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The National University of Engineering (UNI), in the process of assigning vacancies, handled the concept of admission options that allowed those who could not enter in the first time to have a priority, according to their final grade, and be able to compete with their peers to enter in a second, third, fourth and, in some cases, up to the eigth time to the university. The registration system accepted this type of logic supported by the Admission Regulation. This situation led to negative consequences for the UNI and as a result, students who entered the university in the second or later time presented situations such as immediate resignations, not enrolled, postponement of enrollment and untimely resignations. Due to this problem, we proceeded to describe the admission options in the admission processes contemplated in the regulations of the UNI and its implications for student desertion. It was concluded that the UNI modified its admission regulations so that applicants can access careers by vocation and not as a last option for not being out of the system, which resulted in the reduction of student desertion levels.

articleTitle: Motivation increase of mathematics students in Engineering – A proposal from Game Based Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Training and capacity building for students in engineering programs, including developing competencies and skills in mathematics, have been well-established in literature. There is less known about lowering rates of desertion (understood as the non-completion of an academic program). While it is generally agreed that there are multiple causes (individual, institutional, and state), several authors suggest that low academic results and low motivation in an educational process are important causes. In the case of Santo Tomás University, the site of study for this research project, the desertion index in engineering programs is close to 45%. The course with the highest failure rates is introductory mathematics (offered in the first year). Given this context, this research project proposed innovative pedagogical strategies and mediations , targeting the motivation indexes of university-aged students enrolled in mathematics courses. Game-based learning and mixed methods were employed to design a set of two didactic strategies: (A) Kahoot Online Testing Tool, and (B) Online Crossword. The target population was represented by 20 students enrolled in a differential calculus course, as part of the first-year engineering program. For benchmarking purposes, the participants were given a diagnostic calculus test. Next, an adaptation of Instructional Material Motivation Survey was applied, which allowed me to measure the dimensions of attention, confidence, satisfaction, and relevance . The results demonstrated that the pedagogical innovation positively impacted student motivation. The most significant results include the importance of planning rigorous learning activities, incorporating problems from the real student environment, and the importance of offering immediate feedback.

articleTitle: Student results evaluation model: Good practices, lessons learned and challenges to the future
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: This article describes the main characteristics of the evaluation model of student results, model that has been implemented for the preparation of the accreditation process of the Professional School of Systems Engineering of the National University of San Agustin of Arequipa. The model that is described shows a set of good practices oriented to the measurement of the student's results, and observable and measurable actions have been defined through which the development of the competences can be evidenced by means of performance indicators related to the results of the students. In order to define the actions in question, the general and institutional guidelines for the self-evaluation process with a view to accreditation were taken into account. In order to rescue the experiences in the implementation of the proposed model, in the form of lessons learned, highly significant procedures are synthesized in the process of evaluating the student's results. Whereas that assessment is one of the most important aspects of the training process, we propose some future challenges so that they validate the formative design making the evaluation is consistent with the educational objectives and student outcomes.

articleTitle: Professional Profile of Engineering Programs for National Licensing and International Accreditation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: Education in the 21st century faces great challenges mainly due to globalization. The evolution of technologies, including Information and Communication Technologies (ICT), have shortened distances, information are available to all, we know global events immediately, markets are not only local but also global. In this panorama, education also has to evolve to be in accordance with the demands of the 21st century. Education has a new focus, no longer speaking of teaching systems, instead teaching-learning processes. Students must now focus on the achievement of hard skills and soft skills. The most competitive markets demand quality and higher education can't be excluded from this global trend, these is the reason why quality in higher education is accredited through international accreditation agencies. On the other hand, in Peru recently have been implemented reforms, in order to improve the quality of higher education. It has been imposed the licensing process, as a precondition for the provision of services in higher education, both of them for Institutes and Schools of Higher Education and for Universities. In this scenario, engineering and engineering technology programs that aspire to serve the global market, have some difficulties due to licensing at the local level and accreditation requirements at international level. In this paper, we analyze this problem.

articleTitle: Reflections on the Teaching Body Criterion in an accreditation process: Proposal for teaching evaluation from the student perspective
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: In the context of quality evaluation of education, the evaluation of teaching practice is an essential piece if ones consider that students ` results reflect the interaction that takes place during teaching and learning activities. The proposal subject of this work is developed as a result of the self-evaluation, with a view to the accreditation, carried out by the professional School of Systems Engineering of the National University of San Agustin of Arequipa between 2018 and 2019. The structure, for the proposed teaching evaluation, sets the quality criteria and the indicators that conceive the evaluation from the point of view of quality management and relate the quality of the educational institution with the quality of the teacher and the quality of its Activity. Thus, the proposal includes four dimensions that group the competencies that the teacher must possess: Administrative Competencies, Pedagogical Competencies, Investigative Competencies and Training Competencies. The dimensions and factors, proposed for the teaching evaluation, are guided by the policy of continuous improvement, so that for each dimension the factors and indicators that characterize it have been clearly defined. It also offers the steps and details to consider in the design, implementation and analysis of the questionnaire that will be the starting point for the elaboration of the teacher improvement plan. The study carried out has sought to achieve the raised objectives, so its implementation will help the institutional accreditation process.

articleTitle: Research to complete the professional career of engineering – Motivation and facilitation for the initiation of research
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)
abstract: The purpose of this research aims to show a thesis motivation strategy for systems engineering and electronic engineering undergraduates that allow them to obtain their bachelor's degree and professional title according to the three-stage methodology,, first: know the technology developments of companies and universities from developed countries, second: to select research topics taking into account the global development, companies issues and the community of university environment, third: disseminate the selected topics and conduct research on these issues with students in their courses. As a methodology application, two universities were visited, one in Germany and another in the United States; each professor developed a research topics portfolio related to their research lines, professional interest and specialization. Students are able to start their final thesis research when they are at the fifth or sixth level.

Author Keywords: portfolio of research subjects for thesis

articleTitle: The formative research and the methodologies of Learning Based on Problems or Projects (PBL) in the context of the accreditation process
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Engineering Accreditation and Education (ICACIT)

authors.preferredName: Karim Guevara Puente de la Vega

abstract: This article presents the results of the application of the methodologies; problems - based learning (PBL) and projects - based learning (PBL), for the development of formative research, for which the particularities of scientific and formative research are shown, a contextual approach is made for these types of research, then the research proposal in university environments is presented methodologically, finally two cases of application are shown; one for each type of methodology, to conclusively evaluate the results and outline the conclusions with respect to the approach.
